title: Selector Lever Cable Adjustment
introduction:
The selector cable connects the cabin shifter to the transmission’s manual lever. I think of it as a translator: when the cabin says DRIVE, the transmission needs to hear DRIVE too. This adjustment puts both ends in the same position before locking the cable’s adjuster.

The sequence matters: prepare the hoist, position the shifter, disconnect the cable, position the transmission lever, release the adjuster, then reconnect and lock it. The final starting and reverse-lamp checks establish whether the adjustment passes. This is an external cable adjustment, not an internal transmission repair or a fault-isolation guide.

items.name: Prevent an unexpected start
items.detail:
On level ground, select Park, apply the parking brake and chock the wheels against movement in either direction.

If remote start is fitted, disable it through Vehicle settings > Remote Start Setup before working around or underneath the car. Do this while grounded with the controls accessible and before the final ignition-off/key-out step. If display operation needs ignition ON, first establish the current engine-off state: from known OFF, use the pedal-released button press described below; if already ON, leave it ON rather than pressing again.

The Mustang owner manual, Starting and Stopping the Engine, describes the actual keyless controls: with a valid key inside and neither pedal pressed, one press from Off switches the ignition On without starting the engine. From On, one press without the brake switches it Off. Pressing the button with the brake applied requests an engine start, so keep those operations distinct.

Keep the parking brake applied throughout the adjustment. With the ignition OFF, remove the key before lifting or working underneath. Unexpected starting can cause serious injury or death.

items.name: Protect eyes, ears and hands
items.detail: Wear eye and ear protection during service. Wear protective gloves when handling parts with pointed or sharp edges. Failure to follow these precautions may cause serious personal injury.

items.name: Prepare for intentional engine checks
items.detail: Wear eye and hearing protection, and gloves when handling sharp-edged parts. Plan the final engine-start checks in a well-ventilated location; open the garage door before starting and never run the engine in an enclosed space. Keep the car away from dry grass or other combustible ground cover. Relevant service precautions are in [Health and Safety Precautions](#/document/G1693189).

items.name: Keep cabin operations on the ground
items.detail: Complete all cabin selector changes with the vehicle grounded, parking brake applied and wheels chocked. Nobody climbs into the raised cabin. Arrange a gentle prying tool for the adjuster latch; do not force a damaged lock.

items.name: Check capacity and locate the lifting points
items.detail: Use a hoist rated for the vehicle’s weight, including cargo and modifications. The lifting-point drawing identifies reinforced areas along the side sills, behind the front wheels and ahead of the rear wheels. Locate the stamped triangle at each correct lifting point and position the lift arms as shown in [Jacking and Lifting - Overview](#/document/G1663631). Lifting elsewhere can let the vehicle shift or fall, causing serious personal injury; incorrect arm positioning can cause unintended movement, serious personal injury or death.

items.name: Keep hoist hardware clear
items.detail: Position adapters clear of suspension, exhaust and steering linkage components to prevent damage. On a two-column hoist, keep the forks clear of suspension components, mounting brackets and stabilizer mounting brackets, if equipped, and avoid damaging the axle or rear cover.

items.name: If a jack is used during preparation
items.detail: Use a jack with adequate capacity for the vehicle, cargo and modifications, on a hard, level surface at the designated lifting points. Set the parking brake and block every wheel remaining on the ground. After jacking, support the vehicle with floor stands; never get underneath a vehicle supported only by a jack, which can lower unexpectedly. Failure to follow these precautions can cause unintended movement, serious personal injury or death. The supplied emergency jack is only for changing a deflated tire; using it for this job can damage the vehicle. Never apply jack pressure to either bumper, because the bumper covers will be damaged.

edits.why: The adjustment aligns the cabin shifter with the transmission’s manual lever before the cable setting is locked.

edits.text: With the transmission in NEUTRAL, position the vehicle on a hoist. Refer to: [Jacking and Lifting - Overview](#/document/G1663631) (100-02 Jacking and Lifting, Description and Operation).
edits.why:
With the engine stopped, parking brake applied and wheel chocks in place, position the car and hoist adapters at the marked lifting points.

After settings, confirm the engine is stopped and establish the current ignition state. If already On, leave it On. If Off, bring the valid key inside and press the start/stop button once without pressing the brake to obtain engine-off ignition On. Then hold the brake pedal and move the selector from Park to Neutral. The brake shift interlock releases Park with ignition On and the brake applied.

Keep the parking brake applied and the wheels chocked. Release the service brake only after those restraints are established, switch the ignition Off with the button, and remove the key from the vehicle before hands-on adjustment. Neutral does not lock the transmission output shaft.

edits.text: Move the cabin shifter lever to DRIVE.
edits.why: With the car positioned on the hoist but still at ground level, retain the parking brake and wheel chocks. If ignition power is needed, return the valid key inside and establish engine-off ON from known OFF with neither pedal pressed; retain ON if already ON. Hold the service brake and select DRIVE. Confirm the parking brake and chocks secure the car before releasing the service brake; switch ON to OFF without a pedal press, leave an already-OFF ignition OFF, and remove the key. Leave the cabin before lifting. Raise using the specified lifting points and confirm all wheels fully clear and secure hoist support before working underneath. The engine stays off and the parking brake stays applied.

edits.text: Disconnect the selector lever cable end from the transmission’s manual lever. At the cable end beside the ribbed boot, press inward in the sideways arrow’s direction, then move the end downward off the lever attachment as shown.
edits.why: Disconnecting separates the cable setting from the transmission lever position. I use the ribbed boot and the lever’s attachment stud to distinguish this connection from the nearby mounting hardware.

edits.text: Set the transmission’s manual lever to DRIVE using the following movements.
edits.why: The transmission must be in the same selected range as the cabin shifter before the cable is reconnected.

edits.text: Rotate the manual lever clockwise until it reaches its stop.
edits.why: For these rotation directions, face the external manual lever and look toward the transmission case from the cable-connection side. The stop establishes the PARK reference shown in the illustration, giving the following movement a definite starting point.

edits.text: From that stop, rotate the manual lever counterclockwise through 3 detents.
edits.why: Keep that same viewing direction while counting the detents. The detents are the distinct indexed positions felt as the lever moves. This places the transmission lever in DRIVE, matching the cabin shifter.
The adjuster must be free to accommodate the cable position while both levers are set to DRIVE.

edits.text: Gently pry the adjuster latch upward.
edits.why: Lifting the latch releases the restraint on the sliding lock tab; it is a release action, not a reason to force the whole cable end.

edits.text: Push the lock tab downward so it slides into the open position.
edits.why: The tab moves down relative to the adjuster housing in the illustration, freeing the adjustment.
The lower view shows the tab projecting below the housing. Use that position as the visual check before reconnecting the cable.

edits.text: NOTE: After locking the adjuster, pull back on it to confirm that it is securely installed.
edits.why: This checks retention after the tab has been pushed into its locked position; appearance alone is not the final confirmation.

edits.text: Reconnect the cable and lock the adjuster in the following order.
edits.why: The cable connection is made while the adjuster remains released, then the setting is secured.

edits.text: With the adjuster lock tab still released, connect the selector lever cable end to the manual control lever. Move the cable end upward onto the lever attachment as shown.
edits.why: Keeping the tab released allows the connection to settle with both the cabin shifter and transmission lever in DRIVE.

edits.text: Push the lock tab upward to lock the transmission selector lever cable adjustment lock.
edits.why: This secures the established cable setting. Complete the pull-back retention check described in the note before proceeding.

edits.text: Verify that the vehicle starts in PARK and NEUTRAL only, and that the reverse lamps illuminate in REVERSE.
edits.why:
After the adjuster passes its retention check, remove tools and clear everyone underneath. Keep the parking brake applied while lowering; restore wheel chocks as the tires meet the ground before removing hoist support. The selector may still be in DRIVE, so do not rely on the transmission to restrain it. Complete all mechanical work before intentional powered checks.

Perform these checks only with the car fully grounded, parking brake applied and wheels chocked. Keep everyone clear of the car’s front and rear. Provide ventilation, fasten the driver’s belt, switch off headlamps and accessories, and do not press the accelerator.

Bring the valid key inside. From Off, switch ignition On without pressing the brake, then hold the brake and select P. With the brake fully pressed, press the button and verify that the engine starts.

To stop, keep the car stationary in P with the parking brake and chocks holding it, release the service brake and press the button to switch Off.

For the required Neutral check, switch ignition On without the brake, then hold the brake and select N. Press the button with the brake fully applied and verify that the engine starts. Keep the brake held, return to P, then stop the engine using the same restrained, pedal-released shutdown sequence. These keyless operations follow the Mustang owner manual, Starting and Stopping the Engine.

If either required P or N start fails, stop rather than making repeated attempts or continuing to another range. Keep the service brake held and return the stationary selector to P. Confirm Park selection and the fully applied parking brake/chock restraints before releasing the service brake. Establish the engine and ignition state using the ignition-state observations below: switch a known On ignition Off with the pedal-released button press; leave an already-Off ignition Off. Remove the key after confirmed shutdown. If Park, secure restraint or ignition state cannot be established, keep the service brake held and obtain qualified assistance to secure and shut down the vehicle; do not leave the controls. Do not restart testing until the failure is resolved.

Check R, D and S individually with the same grounded restraints, ventilation and clear area. For each check, begin with the engine stopped, selector confirmed in P and ignition confirmed Off. Switch ignition On without pressing the brake, then hold the brake and select the range being checked. Make a brief start request with the button. The engine must not crank or start.

After a no-crank/no-start result, confirm the engine is stopped and establish ignition mode before another button press. The owner manual identifies the START/STOP button indicator as illuminated with ignition On or an engine running; its stationary-shutdown instructions describe stationary shutdown and the extinguished ignition warning lamps/indicators afterward. With the engine stopped, an illuminated button indicator identifies On. If ignition is already Off, leave it Off. If the state is uncertain, stop the test, maintain the service brake and other restraints, and obtain assistance rather than toggling the button blindly.

After a successful inhibited-start check, keep the brake held and return the stationary selector to P. Confirm Park selection and that the fully applied parking brake and wheel chocks secure the car before releasing the service brake. If ignition remains On, release the pedal and press the button once to switch Off; leave an already-Off ignition Off. Confirm Off before setting up the next range.

If the engine unexpectedly cranks or starts, stop the checks. For either outcome, hold the service brake and return the stationary selector to P. Only after Park selection and the parking-brake/chock restraints are confirmed may you release the service brake and use the single pedal-released button press to stop the engine or switch an On ignition Off. Leave an already-Off ignition Off and remove the key after shutdown. If Park cannot be selected or confirmed, or the car cannot be kept secured, do not release the service brake or leave the controls: retain the parking brake and chocks and obtain qualified assistance to secure and shut down the vehicle. Do not continue testing or drive it.

With the engine stopped, the car grounded and the parking brake and wheel chocks still applied, confirm the actual ignition state: leave an already-On engine-off ignition On, or press once from known Off without pressing the brake to obtain On. Then hold the brake and select R. Have a helper observe the reverse lamps from a safe position clear of the vehicle’s travel path. They must illuminate; this check does not require the engine to run.

Hold the brake and return to P. Confirm Park selection and that the parking brake and wheel chocks restrain the car. Only then release the service brake and switch ignition Off. Remove the key from the vehicle after the checks, whether they pass or fail.

If any result requires more cable work, begin that work with ignition Off and the key removed, and repeat the appropriate hoist and restraint sequence.

editorialRevision.scope: Actual owner keyless states, grounded selector/hoist transitions and required P/N-only starting and reverse-lamp checks using prior independently approved control evidence. Adjustment mechanics and three-detent setting unchanged.
